correctness.rationale: Every legal prefix is controlled by the row/column support. An extremal sequence has its penultimate support of exactly m-1 rows and n-1 columns, and every nonfinal edge beyond the first attaches exactly one new bipartite vertex, forming a tree. The last edge gives precisely A/B/C; converses are constructive by growing the tree with the appropriate terminal edge withheld. Bipartite spanning-tree degree enumerator is proved via weighted matrix-tree cofactor and Schur complement; requiring a leaf gives a Stirling surjection subtraction. The detached-edge representation is two-to-one only for 2x2. A standalone exact checker independently enumerates every size-(m+n-2) subset for nine boards, tests closed-neighborhood legality, and compares membership and counts with the formula. Finite checks alone do not prove arbitrary m,n.

originality.rationale: The 2016 Cartesian-product paper already constructs length m+n-2 and is explicitly credited; that numerical lower bound is not claimed new. The principal new claim is the complete three-forest classification of all maximum unordered supports plus their closed Stirling-number census. The 2023 chain-graph primary article and 2024 full rook domination polynomial do not imply the sequential optimization predicate. published-finding corpus searches returned the closest result about complete multipartite graphs, a different family, and no matching rook theorem. Distinct sets counted: 108 on the 3x3 rook graph whereas the published ordinary domination polynomial has 117 dominating four-sets. Residual risk is unindexed equivalent historical work, not erased by failed searches.
residual_risks: Unindexed or preprint-only equivalence under bipartite-forest or line-graph covering-sequence terminology cannot be ruled out.

value.rationale: Rook graphs are canonical line graphs of complete bipartite graphs, and counting all maximum supports is a natural structural strengthening of the previously known one-sequence example. The three-case forest theorem and Stirling-number factors classify an infinite two-parameter extremal family, refining the independently motivated 2024 domination polynomial by the nontrivial sequential legality constraint. The 2x2 boundary prevents double counting. This is neither an arbitrary finite slice nor the routine old lower-bound construction.
